items.why: The report gives a large drop on warming at the higher laser energies ("falls by about 2 decades from 4 K to 295 K at 587 nm and about 1.5 decades at 599 nm") and its areas imply a peak intensity about 10x higher at 4 K (1.09e6 vs 1.1e5). But it frames the change as depending on which side of the resonance you are on, with intensity rising at 623 nm, and never states an overall order-of-magnitude increase on cooling.

It states "The resonance maximum moves from at least 2.11 eV (4 K) to about 2.05 eV (150 K) to about 2.01 eV (295 K)" and ties this to the A-exciton "red-shift of about 0.1 eV from 4 K to 295 K... consistent with the measured resonance movement".
No low-temperature structure (exciton/trion channels, incoming/outgoing resonances) is identified; the report calls the 4 K profile "monotonic with a maximum at the highest laser energy".
Trions and separate exciton/trion resonance amplitudes are never mentioned.

It shows that a fixed-wavelength comparison gives opposite trends "on either side of the resonance", names the exciton resonance as "the dominant effect" on intensities, and notes that four energies "sample the resonance coarsely".
Thin-film interference on SiO2/Si and the need for reflectivity correction are not mentioned; only the cryostat window, focus and Si throughput variation are raised.
It asks: "Was a power series at 4 K... or a Stokes/anti-Stokes measurement made to estimate the laser-heated local temperature?"

wrong_claims.why: The Bose-Einstein factor is never invoked; the intensity change is put down to the exciton resonance.
The report says the maximum moves to lower energy on warming, which means higher energy on cooling (the correct direction).
